newsitem.title: USA: US Mid-Atlantic spot power prices steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: US Mid-Atlantic spot power prices steady to higher.

text.p: Day-ahead bulk electricity prices in Mid-Atlantic U.S. rose Wednesday after recent losses amid talk of transmission constraint in the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect pool.
Market sources surveyed could not attribute a particular reason for a split in the system.
"There's load constraint that aggrevated the condition," said one PJM electricity trader.
The pool's peak demand for today was projected at 34,200 megawatts (MW), down almost 1,500 MW from Tuesday.

The dispatch rate in the eastern half of PJM, where more oil and natural gas generation is concentrated, was assessed at $26.50 a megawatt hour (MWh). The production cost in western PJM, which is generally cheaper because of more coal generation, was valued at $16.25, market sources said.

Firm, peak PJM electricity for Thursday (excluding transmission costs) was traded in a $3.50 range. Most deals changed hands between $24.00 and $25.50 a megawatt hour (MWh), up from Tuesday's $22.00-$23.50 for delivery today.
Firm, off-peak PJM power for Thursday was notionally valued at $16.00-$17.00, up from $15.00-$16.00 Tuesday.

Forecasts showed the region would enjoy mild weather for the next couple of days with readings running five to eight degrees F above normal. Temperatures would cool near normal levels this weekends before climbing again Monday.
PJM firm, peak electricity for delivery next week rose to $28.00-30.00 from Tuesday's $26.25-28.00. Some forecasts still called for an arctic blast to hit the eastern U.S. next week.
Balance-of-February PJM power climbed to $28.50-29.50 from $27.50-29.00 Tuesday.
March PJM deliveries firmed to $24.10-24.45 from Tuesday's quote of $24.00-24.20.
PJM prices for April and May widened to $21.95-22.20 from $22.05-22.15 Tuesday. June PJM electricity remained at $24.90-25.15.
July/August PJM power was better bid at $30.25-30.45 from Tuesday's $30.10-30.45.
PJM third-quarter electricity edged up to $27.90-28.10 from $27.80-28.05 Tuesday, and fourth-quarter PJM prices tightened to a range of $23.85-24.00 from Tuesday's $23.80-24.10.
Firm, peak PJM deliveries for 1998 held at $25.50-25.95.

Swing natural gas prices at the Philadelphia city gate were flat from Tuesday's level after edging higher in early trading. Gas deliveries for Thursday were reportedly done in a $2.90-3.00 per million British thermal unit range.
As of 1247 EST, NYMEX March Henry Hub gas futures fell 6.2 cents at $2.435/mmBtu.
